messages:
alicia: Heads-up — p95 for /v1/generate spiked from 120ms -> 420ms around 13:08 UTC. Console shows a routing fallback to the cheaper variant at the same time. Not sure if our percentile calc is attributing correctly. :thinking:
ben: link? can you grab the console permalink and the raw samples?
alicia: console: https://console.redwood/latency?endpoint=/v1/generate&range=1h :point_up: raw samples attached (copied snippet below).
---
# sample rows (time, route, latency_ms, sample_origin)
2026-03-22T13:07:41Z route=primary latency_ms=118 origin=client
2026-03-22T13:08:02Z route=fallback latency_ms=430 origin=server
2026-03-22T13:08:03Z route=fallback latency_ms=412 origin=server
2026-03-22T13:08:07Z route=primary latency_ms=125 origin=client
---
sam: quick theory: fallback requests are marked origin=server (because routed downstream) and our p95 view currently shows a blended percentile but the legend says "client-origin only" sometimes. UI/metadata mismatch?
priya: also check KV cache hits — fallback path might bypass cache so tail gets worse. If fallback amplifies non-cached requests, p95 will jump even if primary path is fine.
jordan: can you run the query with split by `route` and `sample_origin` and include the `include_retries` flag? curious if retries are inflating tail. eg:
```
SELECT quantile(0.95)(latency_ms) as p95, route, sample_origin
FROM latency_samples
WHERE endpoint='/v1/generate' AND time > now() - interval '15 minutes'
GROUP BY route, sample_origin;
```
alicia: running now — results incoming. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
telemetry-bot: query job 43912 started by alicia.
alicia: results: primary/client p95=130ms, fallback/server p95=418ms, fallback/client p95=390ms (small n=14). console p95 (blended) was 420ms. So blended number mostly from fallback.
ben: sounds like expected math but UX is confusing — console label didn't show that route split existed. we should either auto-annotate fallback-weight or show sample counts next to percentiles.
priya: agree. proposal: show per-route p50/p95/p99 rows with sample_count and a tooltip explaining sample_origin (client/server/retry).
sam: short-term: add a badge on the overall percentile chart "high fallback contribution" when >30% of tail comes from non-primary routes. simple heuristic.
jordan: also add a dataset disclaimer when sample_count < 100 that pctl is noisy. the fallback had n=14 for client-route. noisy. :warning:
alicia: i'll file a quick console issue and add the query + raw rows. owner: alicia. action items: console UX tweak (ben), badge heuristic (sam), KV-cache investigation (priya), docs blurb about sample_origin (jordan).
ben: assign me for the UX ticket, will sketch a small mock tomorrow. :+1:
priya: i'll start KV cache logs check and reuse heatmap we already have.
sam: i'll prototype the fallback badge rule and add unit tests for the heuristic.
jordan: i'll write the sample_count advisory text for the tooltip.
alicia: thanks all. marking this thread resolved unless anything else shows up in the next hour. :white_check_mark:
